title: Seal a filled zip-top bag: hold its mouth's corner and pinch-slide the press-to-seal track shut corner to corner
context: Bagging prepped vegetables, portions and leftovers in zip-top freezer bags is routine for food preparation workers (about 900,000 in the US) and cooks, and one of the commonest household kitchen jobs. A press-to-seal track has no slider: it closes only where it is squeezed between finger and thumb. So one hand holds the mouth's corner while the other pinches the track beside it and slides along to the far corner; slid without the held corner, the pinch drags and slews the bag over the board.
setup: Counter top is z = 0.7475 m (x away from the arms, y to the left). Objects, all real size: (1) Butcher block, fixed: end-grain maple (drawn with a wood texture), 12 x 18 x 1 3/4 in (305 x 457 x 45 mm), centred at x 0.3875, y 0.02 m, near edge x 0.235, with a juice groove round its top. (2) Zip-top bag, free rigid body, 320 g: a 1-quart freezer bag, 177 x 188 mm outside (6 15/16 x 7 3/8 in), 0.1 mm LDPE films, filled 30 mm deep with about 300 g of chopped carrot coins (17 mm across), pepper pieces (about 18 x 10 x 5 mm) and celery pieces (20 x 8 x 6 mm), lying on the block, mouth toward the arms, centreline y 0. Its press-to-seal track (polyethylene) runs along y across the full 177 mm width at x 0.205, 10 mm in from the mouth's edge and 30 mm out past the block's near edge: a blue rib profile on the top film (4 mm wide, 1.6 mm thick) lying 3 mm clear above the yellow groove profile on the bottom film (2.6 mm thick pressed home), as left open. (3) Chef's knife, fixed: 8 in stainless steel blade (200 x 42 x 2.2 mm) and black polymer handle (120 x 24 x 16 mm), lying flat on the block's right side, blade centred at x 0.378, y -0.14, tip toward the arms. (4) Vegetable ends, fixed, on the block's left side around x 0.48, y 0.175: a carrot top (cone 24 mm across, 30 mm long), a pepper stem (8 mm across, 12 mm long), a pepper core piece (30 x 20 x 12 mm) and a celery end (24 x 12 x 10 mm). (5) Prep bowl, fixed: 1.5-qt stainless steel bowl, 200 mm across the rim, 85 mm deep, holding chopped vegetables, at x 0.645, y 0.20 on the counter. (6) Bag carton, fixed: printed paperboard carton of quart freezer bags, 190 x 75 x 95 mm, open at the top with a bag showing, at x 0.66, y -0.20 on the counter.
scoring: The track is 16 cells of 11 mm. 0.25: at least 4 cells closed. 0.5: at least 12. 0.75: all 16 closed with the bag never dragged more than 10 mm over the block nor turned more than 5 degrees, and never tipped past 15 degrees while still open (the load spills). 1.0: also both hands' tool centres at least 80 mm from the track for 1 s. Dragging or turning the bag past those limits, or spilling, caps the score at 0.5.
reset_notes: Fixed starting poses, no randomisation: block, bag (track open, all cells open), knife, scraps, bowl and carton as listed; arms at the ready pose.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The filled bag is one rigid body (load, film edges, track); film does not crease or stretch, and the clear film is drawn by its edges. Closing is a rule: a track cell closes where a hand's pads are squeezed across it to within 1 mm of the pressed-home 2.6 mm (open: 6.2 mm), closing line within 30 degrees of the films' normal; it then reads green. The pads touch the groove profile (friction 0.15), so a clamped pinch slid along the track drags the bag by friction unless it is held.
